subproblem.title: Cauchy subsequence in flat distance from finite ε-nets (pigeonhole and diagonal argument)
subproblem.statement: Conventions: ℝ^P = Euclid P and Hᵈ = μHE[d]. For U ⊆ ℝ^P, 𝒟^d(U) = TestFormOn U d (smooth d-forms on ℝ^P with compact support contained in U) and 𝒟_d(U) = GeometricCurrentOn U d; ∂X = X.boundary (∂X(ω) = X(dω)); X − Y is the contract subtraction (pointwise on test forms). For G ⊆ ℝ^P, M_G(X) = X.massOn G is the supremum of max(X(ω), 0) over ω ∈ 𝒟^d(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ G and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x, where |·| is the Euclidean coefficient norm of covectors (covectorEuclideanNorm); M(X) = X.mass = M_U(X). An IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) in U is the contract structure IMRep U d; R represents X when X(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHᵈ for every ω ∈ 𝒟^d(U), where ⟨ω, ξ⟩(x) = ξ(x)(ω(x)); μ_R = θ·Hᵈ⌞M is R.measure; X is integer multiplicity (IM, IsIntegerMultiplicity X) if some IMRep represents it. X vanishes off a set K if X(ω) = 0 for every ω whose tsupport is disjoint from K. X_j ⇀ Y (WeaklyConvergesOn) means X_j(ω) → Y(ω) for every ω. V ⊂⊂ U (CompactlyContained V U) means that closure V is compact and contained in U. Let P, m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, U ⊆ ℝ^P open and X_j ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (j ∈ ℕ). Suppose that for every ε ∈ (0, ∞] there is a finite set 𝒬 ⊆ 𝒟_n(U) such that for every j there are Q ∈ 𝒬 and IM R ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(U), S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with X_j(ω) − Q(ω) = ∂R(ω) + S(ω) for all ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) and M(R) + M(S) < ε. Then there is a strictly increasing θ : ℕ → ℕ such that for every r ∈ ℕ there are IM R_r ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(U), S_r ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with X_{θ(r+1)}(ω) − X_{θ(r)}(ω) = ∂R_r(ω) + S_r(ω) for all ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) and M(R_r) + M(S_r) ≤ 2^{−r} (that is, (2⁻¹)^r in [0, ∞]).

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 of the parent-supplied proof (Simon Ch. 6, proof of Theorem 7.2: 'apply (1) with ε = 1, 1/2, 1/4 etc. to extract a subsequence {T_{j_r}} with d(T_{j_{r+1}}, T_{j_r}) < 2^{−r}', chapter-06.txt lines 2103–2117). Tool: the sibling (IMC) the reused accepted sibling cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub: (a) if U is open, M ⊆ M' ⊆ U are Borel and Hᵈ(M' ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, then for Hᵈ-a.e. x ∈ M and every linear subspace Q, M has approximate tangent space Q at x iff M' has (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt d · x Q); (b) if U is open, R = (M, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in U and E is Borel, there are A ∈ 𝒟_d(U) and an IMRep R' in U with carrier M ∩ E, multiplicity θ and orientation ξ that represents A (so μ_{R'} = μ_R⌞E); (c) if U is open and A, B ∈ 𝒟_d(U) are IM, then A − B is IM; (d) for every IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) in any U and Hᵈ-a.e. x ∈ M, |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for every d-covector α.
1. Mass of a difference. For A, B ∈ 𝒟_d(U), M(A − B) ≤ M(A) + M(B): if ω is admissible for M_U then so is −ω, and (A − B)(ω) = A(ω) + B(−ω) ≤ M(A) + M(B).
2. Choices. For r ∈ ℕ let ε_r := 2^{−r−1} > 0 and let 𝒬_r be a finite set given by the hypothesis for ε_r. For every r and j choose Q_r(j) ∈ 𝒬_r and IM R_r(j) ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(U), S_r(j) ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with X_j − Q_r(j) = ∂R_r(j) + S_r(j) on 𝒟ⁿ(U) and M(R_r(j)) + M(S_r(j)) < ε_r.
3. Nested infinite index sets (pigeonhole). Put J_{−1} := ℕ. If J_{r−1} ⊆ ℕ is infinite, the map j ↦ Q_r(j) on J_{r−1} takes values in the finite set 𝒬_r, so some value q_r has an infinite fibre (Finite.exists_infinite_fiber); let J_r := {j ∈ J_{r−1} : Q_r(j) = q_r}. This gives infinite sets J_0 ⊇ J_1 ⊇ J_2 ⊇ ⋯ with Q_r(j) = q_r for all j ∈ J_r.
4. Diagonal choice. Choose θ(0) ∈ J_0 and, inductively, θ(r + 1) ∈ J_{r+1} with θ(r + 1) > θ(r) (possible since J_{r+1} is infinite). Then θ is strictly increasing and θ(r), θ(r + 1) ∈ J_r for every r (as J_{r+1} ⊆ J_r).
5. Differences. Fix r, put j := θ(r), j' := θ(r + 1), so Q_r(j) = Q_r(j') = q_r. Let R_r := R_r(j') − R_r(j) and S_r := S_r(j') − S_r(j) (contract subtraction); both are IM by (IMC)(c). For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), using ∂(A − B)(ω) = A(dω) − B(dω): X_{j'}(ω) − X_j(ω) = (q_r(ω) + R_r(j')(dω) + S_r(j')(ω)) − (q_r(ω) + R_r(j)(dω) + S_r(j)(ω)) = ∂R_r(ω) + S_r(ω). By step 1, M(R_r) + M(S_r) ≤ M(R_r(j')) + M(S_r(j')) + M(R_r(j)) + M(S_r(j)) < 2ε_r = 2^{−r}. ∎
proof_key_steps: Mass of a difference is at most the sum of the masses (−ω is admissible whenever ω is).
For ε_r = 2^{−r−1} pick the finite net 𝒬_r and a decomposition X_j − Q_r(j) = ∂R + S for every j.
Pigeonhole gives nested infinite index sets J_r on which Q_r(j) is a fixed q_r; choose θ(r) ∈ J_r increasing.
Subtracting the two decompositions of X_{θ(r+1)} and X_{θ(r)} with the same q_r gives IM R_r, S_r ((IMC)(c)) with mass < 2ε_r = 2^{−r}.

audit.reason: The finite-net hypothesis and dyadic conclusion match exactly. Nested infinite fibres yield a strictly increasing diagonal sequence. Subtracting decompositions with a common center produces IM differences and the required mass bound; neither the parent theorem nor integer multiplicity of the centers is assumed.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, Lemma 3.13 and its printed proof (chapter-06.txt lines 901–935), applied to the partial sums Y_q = X_0 + ⋯ + X_{q−1}, which are Cauchy for the mass M; the steps the printed proof leaves implicit (that the densities θ_qξ_q converge in L¹, that the limit multiplicity is an integer, and the identification of approximate tangent planes) are written out. Tools: the siblings (C1) the reused accepted sibling dor_imrep_massOn_eq_measure_and_support: for open U, X ∈ 𝒟_d(U) and an IMRep R in U representing X, M_W(X) = μ_R(W) for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P, and spt X = U ∩ spt μ_R. and (IMC) the reused accepted sibling cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub: (a) if U is open, M ⊆ M' ⊆ U are Borel and Hᵈ(M' ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, then for Hᵈ-a.e. x ∈ M and every linear subspace Q, M has approximate tangent space Q at x iff M' has (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt d · x Q); (b) if U is open, R = (M, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in U and E is Borel, there are A ∈ 𝒟_d(U) and an IMRep R' in U with carrier M ∩ E, multiplicity θ and orientation ξ that represents A (so μ_{R'} = μ_R⌞E); (c) if U is open and A, B ∈ 𝒟_d(U) are IM, then A − B is IM; (d) for every IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) in any U and Hᵈ-a.e. x ∈ M, |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for every d-covector α. (UOD) the reused accepted sibling dor_ims_unitOrientation_dual: for all P, n there is a continuous linear map L from n-vectors to n-covectors such that for every n-vector ξ and subspace Q with IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q: |ξ(α)| ≤ |α| for every n-covector α, |L(ξ)| ≤ 1 and ξ(L(ξ)) = 1. The zero current of any degree d in any U is IM: the IMRep with carrier ∅, multiplicity 0 and orientation 0 represents it (∅ is Borel and countably d-rectifiable by Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.countablyRectifiable_of_measure_zero, and every integral or a.e. condition over ∅ holds trivially). For X ∈ 𝒟_d(U), ω ∈ 𝒟^d(U) and an open (or arbitrary) G ⊇ tsupport ω: |X(ω)| ≤ ‖ω‖·M_G(X), where ‖ω‖ := sup_x |ω(x)| < ∞. Indeed if ‖ω‖ = 0 then ω = 0 (|·| is a norm: an alternating map vanishing on all increasing tuples of standard basis vectors is 0), and otherwise ±ω/‖ω‖ are admissible for M_G(X). Notation: for an n-vector ζ (MultiVector P n, a continuous linear functional on n-covectors) let |ζ|* := sup{ζ(α) : |α| ≤ 1}, the dual norm; ⟨ω, ζ⟩(x) := ζ(x)(ω(x)); Hⁿ := μHE[n]; Λ := Σ_r M(X_r) < ∞.
1. The current Y. By the mass inequality, Σ_r |X_r(ω)| ≤ ‖ω‖Λ < ∞, so Y(ω) := Σ_r X_r(ω) is an absolutely convergent series (HasSum), linear in ω. If ω_k → 0 in 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOnConverges ω_k 0), then ω_k → 0 uniformly (the derivative of order 0), hence ‖ω_k‖ → 0 (all norms on the finite-dimensional space of covectors are equivalent), and |Y(ω_k)| ≤ ‖ω_k‖Λ → 0; so Y ∈ 𝒟_n(U). If ω is admissible for M(Y) = M_U(Y), then Y(ω) = Σ_r X_r(ω) ≤ Σ_r M(X_r), so M(Y) ≤ Σ_r M(X_r). It remains to show that Y is IM.
2. Densities of the X_r. Fix IMReps R_r = (M_r, θ_r, ξ_r) of X_r. For Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M_r, ξ_r(x) is a unit orientation of a subspace (IMRep.orients), so by (UOD) |ξ_r(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all α and ξ_r(x)(L(ξ_r(x))) = 1 with |L(ξ_r(x))| ≤ 1; hence |ξ_r(x)|* = 1. More generally |ζ|* = 1 for every unit orientation ζ of a subspace. Put η_r := θ_rξ_r on M_r and η_r := 0 off M_r. Then X_r(ω) = ∫⟨ω, η_r⟩ dHⁿ, and by (C1) ∫|η_r|* dHⁿ = ∫_{M_r} θ_r dHⁿ = μ_{R_r}(U) = M(X_r). Let E := ⋃_r M_r (Borel, countably n-rectifiable). By monotone convergence ∫ Σ_r|η_r|* dHⁿ = Λ < ∞, so η := Σ_r η_r converges absolutely Hⁿ-a.e., η = 0 off E, ∫|η|* dHⁿ ≤ Λ, and by dominated convergence (dominating function ‖ω‖Σ_r|η_r|*) Y(ω) = Σ_r∫⟨ω, η_r⟩ dHⁿ = ∫⟨ω, η⟩ dHⁿ for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U).

By the remark on zero currents and (IMC)(c), every Y_q is IM; fix an IMRep R'_q = (N_q, ϑ_q, ζ_q) of Y_q and put η'_q := ϑ_qζ_q on N_q, 0 off N_q; as in step 2, |ζ_q|* = 1 Hⁿ-a.e. on N_q. Z := H_q − η'_q vanishes off A_q, is locally ν_q-integrable on U, and ∫⟨ω, Z⟩ dν_q = Y_q(ω) − Y_q(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). 6. Orientation. For x ∈ M₊ and q ≥ q₀(x): ϑ_q(x)1_{N_q}(x) = θ(x) ≥ 1, so x ∈ N_q, ϑ_q(x) = θ(x) and ζ_q(x) = η'_q(x)/θ(x) = H_q(x)/θ(x) → η(x)/θ(x) = ξ(x). For x ∈ M₊ ∖ Z₁ and q ≥ q₀(x), N_q has an approximate tangent space Q_x at x of which ζ_q(x) is a unit orientation (IMRep.orients for R'_q), so M₊ has the approximate tangent space Q_x at x (it is unique, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique, so Q_x does not depend on q), and all ζ_q(x), q ≥ q₀(x), lie in the two-point set {e_x, −e_x}, e_x := τ₁∧⋯∧τ_n for one fixed orthonormal basis τ of Q_x (two orthonormal bases of Q_x differ by an orthogonal matrix of determinant ±1). subproblem.statement: Assume (SL) the exact frozen statement of dor_lmb_slicing_lipschitz (a dependency of the parent node), taken as an antecedent: assuming (C1), for every open U ⊆ ℝ^P, every T ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(U) represented by an IMRep RT = (M, θ, ξ), every IMRep RB = (M', θ', ξ') representing ∂T and every L-Lipschitz f : ℝ^P → ℝ, there are P_t ∈ 𝒟_k(U) (t ∈ ℝ) such that (1) for every open W, t ↦ M_W(P_t) is a.e.-measurable and ∫_ℝ M_W(P_t) dt ≤ L·M_W(T); (2) for L¹-a.e. t: P_t is IM, P_t(ω) = 0 for every ω whose tsupport is disjoint from f⁻¹(t), and P_t(ω) = ∫_{M∩{f<t}} θ⟨dω, ξ⟩ dH^{k+1} − ∫_{M'∩{f<t}} θ'⟨ω, ξ'⟩ dH^k for every ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U). Conventions: ℝ^P = Euclid P and Hᵈ = μHE[d]. For U ⊆ ℝ^P, 𝒟^d(U) = TestFormOn U d (smooth d-forms on ℝ^P with compact support contained in U) and 𝒟_d(U) = GeometricCurrentOn U d; ∂X = X.boundary (∂X(ω) = X(dω)); X − Y is the contract subtraction (pointwise on test forms). For G ⊆ ℝ^P, M_G(X) = X.massOn G is the supremum of max(X(ω), 0) over ω ∈ 𝒟^d(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ G and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x, where |·| is the Euclidean coefficient norm of covectors (covectorEuclideanNorm); M(X) = X.mass = M_U(X). An IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) in U is the contract structure IMRep U d; R represents X when X(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHᵈ for every ω ∈ 𝒟^d(U), where ⟨ω, ξ⟩(x) = ξ(x)(ω(x)); μ_R = θ·Hᵈ⌞M is R.measure; X is integer multiplicity (IM, IsIntegerMultiplicity X) if some IMRep represents it. X vanishes off a set K if X(ω) = 0 for every ω whose tsupport is disjoint from K. X_j ⇀ Y (WeaklyConvergesOn) means X_j(ω) → Y(ω) for every ω. V ⊂⊂ U (CompactlyContained V U) means that closure V is compact and contained in U. Let P, m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, and let T_j (j ∈ ℕ) and T be IM currents in 𝒟_n(U) with ∂T_j = 0 for every j, sup_j M_V(T_j) < ∞ for every open V ⊂⊂ U, and T_j ⇀ T in U. Let W ⊆ ℝ^P be nonempty with W ⊂⊂ U. Then there are a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ, a compact K ⊆ U, Λ ∈ [0, ∞) and currents T'_j (j ∈ ℕ), T' ∈ 𝒟_n(U) such that: every T'_j, every ∂T'_j and T' are IM; every T'_j vanishes off K; M(T'_j) ≤ Λ and M(∂T'_j) ≤ Λ for every j; T'_j ⇀ T' in U; and T'_j(ω) = T_{φ(j)}(ω) and T'(ω) = T(ω) for every j and every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W. subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the parent-supplied proof (Simon Ch. 6, proof of Theorem 7.2, chapter-06.txt lines 2091–2102: 'by 4.5(1),(2) and an argument as in 6.7(2) of Ch. 2 ... we can assume ... spt T_j ⊆ W̄'), with the parent's correction that the cutting level is chosen so that the localized currents converge weakly to the localized limit. Tools: (SL); the siblings (C1) the reused accepted sibling dor_imrep_massOn_eq_measure_and_support: for open U, X ∈ 𝒟_d(U) and an IMRep R in U representing X, M_W(X) = μ_R(W) for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P, and spt X = U ∩ spt μ_R. and (IMC) the reused accepted sibling cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub: (a) if U is open, M ⊆ M' ⊆ U are Borel and Hᵈ(M' ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, then for Hᵈ-a.e. x ∈ M and every linear subspace Q, M has approximate tangent space Q at x iff M' has (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt d · x Q); (b) if U is open, R = (M, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in U and E is Borel, there are A ∈ 𝒟_d(U) and an IMRep R' in U with carrier M ∩ E, multiplicity θ and orientation ξ that represents A (so μ_{R'} = μ_R⌞E); (c) if U is open and A, B ∈ 𝒟_d(U) are IM, then A − B is IM; (d) for every IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) in any U and Hᵈ-a.e. x ∈ M, |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for every d-covector α. The zero current of any degree d in any U is IM: the IMRep with carrier ∅, multiplicity 0 and orientation 0 represents it (∅ is Borel and countably d-rectifiable by Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.countablyRectifiable_of_measure_zero, and every integral or a.e. condition over ∅ holds trivially). For X ∈ 𝒟_d(U), ω ∈ 𝒟^d(U) and an open (or arbitrary) G ⊇ tsupport ω: |X(ω)| ≤ ‖ω‖·M_G(X), where ‖ω‖ := sup_x |ω(x)| < ∞. Indeed if ‖ω‖ = 0 then ω = 0 (|·| is a norm: an alternating map vanishing on all increasing tuples of standard basis vectors is 0), and otherwise ±ω/‖ω‖ are admissible for M_G(X).
1. Setup. Let f(x) := dist(x, W̄) (Metric.infDist x (closure W)); f is 1-Lipschitz (lipschitz_infDist_pt), f = 0 on W̄, and since W̄ is compact and nonempty, {f ≤ r} = cthickening(r, W̄) is compact for r ≥ 0. As W̄ is a compact subset of the open set U, choose δ > 0 with {f ≤ 3δ} ⊆ U (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open). W'' := {f < 3δ} is open, closure W'' ⊆ {f ≤ 3δ} ⊆ U is compact, so W'' ⊂⊂ U and Λ₀ := sup_j M_{W''}(T_j) < ∞. Fix IMReps R_j = (M_j, θ_j, ξ_j) of T_j and R_∞ = (M, θ, ξ) of T, and put μ_j := μ_{R_j}, μ := μ_{R_∞}. By (C1), μ_j(G) = M_G(T_j) and μ(G) = M_G(T) for every open G; in particular μ_j(W'') ≤ Λ₀, and μ(W'') ≤ ∫_{M∩{f≤3δ}} θ dHⁿ < ∞ by the local integrability of θ on the compact {f ≤ 3δ} ⊆ U.
2. Monotone functions. For s ∈ [δ, 3δ] put g_j(s) := μ_j({f < s}) ∈ [0, Λ₀]; each g_j is nondecreasing. Let D := ℚ ∩ (δ, 3δ) (countable, dense). By Bolzano–Weierstrass in [0, Λ₀] (IsCompact.tendsto_subseq) and a diagonal argument over an enumeration of D there is a strictly increasing φ₁ such that G(q) := lim_j g_{φ₁(j)}(q) exists for every q ∈ D; G is nondecreasing on D. For s ∈ (δ, 3δ) put G⁻(s) := sup{G(q) : q ∈ D, q < s} and G⁺(s) := inf{G(q) : q ∈ D, q > s}; G⁻ ≤ G⁺ and G⁻ is nondecreasing, so the set C of s with G⁻(s) < G⁺(s) is countable (the intervals (G⁻(s), G⁺(s)) are pairwise disjoint and each contains a rational; equivalently C is contained in the discontinuity set of the monotone function G⁻, Monotone.countable_not_continuousAt). If s ∉ C, monotonicity gives g_j(q) ≤ g_j(s) ≤ g_j(q') for q < s < q' in D, so lim_j g_{φ₁(j)}(s) exists and equals G(s) := G⁻(s) = G⁺(s), and G(q) → G(s) as q ↑ s, q ∈ D.
3. Slices. For each j apply (SL), with (C1) from the sibling, to T_{φ₁(j)} ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(U), RT := R_{φ₁(j)}, RB := the empty IMRep in degree m (it represents the zero current, which is ∂T_{φ₁(j)} by hypothesis), f and L := 1. This gives P_{j,s} ∈ 𝒟_m(U), s ∈ ℝ, with (i) s ↦ M_{W''}(P_{j,s}) a.e.-measurable and ∫_ℝ M_{W''}(P_{j,s}) ds ≤ M_{W''}(T_{φ₁(j)}) ≤ Λ₀; (ii) for a.e. s: P_{j,s} is IM, P_{j,s}(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ∩ f⁻¹(s) = ∅, and P_{j,s}(ω) = ∫_{M_{φ₁(j)}∩{f<s}} θ_{φ₁(j)}⟨dω, ξ_{φ₁(j)}⟩ dH^{m+1} for every ω ∈ 𝒟^m(U) (the RB-integral is over the empty set). By Fatou's lemma for a.e.-measurable functions (lintegral_liminf_le'), ∫_ℝ liminf_j M_{W''}(P_{j,s}) ds ≤ liminf_j ∫_ℝ M_{W''}(P_{j,s}) ds ≤ Λ₀ < ∞. The function s ↦ liminf_j M_{W''}(P_{j,s}) is a.e.-measurable (it agrees a.e. with the liminf of the measurable modifications AEMeasurable.mk, which is measurable by Measurable.liminf), so finiteness of its integral gives liminf_j M_{W''}(P_{j,s}) < ∞ for a.e. s (ae_lt_top').
4. Choice of the level t. The set of s ∈ (δ, 2δ) with (a) s ∉ C, (b) (ii) holds at s for every j, (c) liminf_j M_{W''}(P_{j,s}) < ∞ has full Lebesgue measure in (δ, 2δ): C is countable, (b) is a countable intersection of conull sets (ae_all_iff), and (c) holds a.e. by step 3. Fix such a t. By (c) there is a strictly increasing φ₂ with M_{W''}(P_{φ₂(j),t}) ≤ Λ₁ := liminf_j M_{W''}(P_{j,t}) + 1 < ∞ for every j. Put φ := φ₁ ∘ φ₂ (strictly increasing), W₁ := {f < t} (open, W ⊆ W̄ ⊆ W₁ since t > 0), K := {f ≤ t} (compact, K ⊆ {f ≤ 3δ} ⊆ U) and Λ := max(Λ₀, Λ₁). Note that g_{φ(j)} = g_{φ₁(φ₂(j))} still converges to G at t and on D.
5. The localized currents. For each j apply (IMC)(b) to R_{φ(j)} and E := W₁: this gives T'_j ∈ 𝒟_n(U) represented by the IMRep R'_j with carrier M_{φ(j)} ∩ W₁, multiplicity θ_{φ(j)} and orientation ξ_{φ(j)}; so T'_j is IM and μ_{R'_j} = μ_{φ(j)}⌞W₁. Likewise T' ∈ 𝒟_n(U) is represented by (M ∩ W₁, θ, ξ), is IM, and μ_{R'_∞} = μ⌞W₁.
 (i) T'_j vanishes off K: if tsupport ω ∩ K = ∅ then ω = 0 on W₁ ⊆ K, so T'_j(ω) = ∫_{M_{φ(j)}∩W₁} θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ = 0.
 (ii) Agreement on W: if tsupport ω ⊆ W then ω = 0 outside W₁, so T'_j(ω) = ∫_{M_{φ(j)}} θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ = T_{φ(j)}(ω), and likewise T'(ω) = T(ω).
 (iii) Boundary: for ω ∈ 𝒟^m(U), ∂T'_j(ω) = T'_j(dω) = ∫_{M_{φ(j)}∩{f<t}} θ_{φ(j)}⟨dω, ξ_{φ(j)}⟩ dH^{m+1} = P_{φ₂(j),t}(ω) by step 3(ii) at s = t (the index φ₂(j) of the φ₁-subsequence is the index φ(j) of the original sequence). Hence ∂T'_j = P_{φ₂(j),t} (GeometricCurrentOn.ext) is IM.
 (iv) Masses: M(T'_j) = μ_{R'_j}(U) = μ_{φ(j)}(W₁) ≤ μ_{φ(j)}(W'') = M_{W''}(T_{φ(j)}) ≤ Λ₀ by (C1) (W₁ ⊆ W''). 1. The retraction (Lemma 5.4). Erratum: the printed proof of the derivative bound (3) is wrong, see (1g). Parts (1a)–(1f) below keep the printed construction of ψ and replace that proof. Fix a ∈ B_{1/4}(q); then a_i ∈ (1/4, 3/4) for every i, because |a_i − 1/2| ≤ |a − q| < 1/4.
 (1a) Skeleta. A point lies in L_j iff at least P − j of its coordinates are integers: a j-face z + F has P − j fixed integer coordinates; conversely, fix P − j integer coordinates of the point and choose unit intervals containing the others. Hence L_{ℓ−1}(a) = {x : x_i − a_i ∈ ℤ for at least n + 1 indices i}. This is a closed ℤ^P-periodic set, the complete periodic lattice. Since |x_i − a_i| < 1 for x ∈ C, its local arrangement in C is Λ(a) := C ∩ L_{ℓ−1}(a) = {x ∈ C : x_i = a_i for at least n + 1 indices i}. Also dist(L_{ℓ−1}(a), L_n) ≥ 1/4. Indeed, let w ∈ L_n and w' ∈ L_{ℓ−1}(a). At least ℓ coordinates of w are integers and at least n + 1 coordinates of w' − a are integers. As ℓ + n + 1 > P, some index i has w_i ∈ ℤ and w'_i ∈ a_i + ℤ, so |w − w'| ≥ dist(a_i, ℤ) > 1/4.

 - Since h_i(x) ∈ (1/4, 3/4), δ_i ≤ r_i ≤ 4δ_i.

1. Tails. Fix ℓ. For every r, M(R_{ℓ+r}) ≤ 2^{−ℓ−r} and M(S_{ℓ+r}) ≤ 2^{−ℓ−r}, so Σ_r M(R_{ℓ+r}) ≤ Σ_r 2^{−ℓ−r} = 2·2^{−ℓ} < ∞ and likewise Σ_r M(S_{ℓ+r}) < ∞ (ENNReal.tsum_geometric).

Also (C1) the reused accepted sibling dor_imrep_massOn_eq_measure_and_support: for open U, X ∈ 𝒟_d(U) and an IMRep R in U representing X, M_W(X) = μ_R(W) for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P, and spt X = U ∩ spt μ_R. (IMC) the reused accepted sibling cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub: (a) if U is open, M ⊆ M' ⊆ U are Borel and Hᵈ(M' ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, then for Hᵈ-a.e. x ∈ M and every linear subspace Q, M has approximate tangent space Q at x iff M' has (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt d · x Q); (b) if U is open, R = (M, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in U and E is Borel, there are A ∈ 𝒟_d(U) and an IMRep R' in U with carrier M ∩ E, multiplicity θ and orientation ξ that represents A (so μ_{R'} = μ_R⌞E); (c) if U is open and A, B ∈ 𝒟_d(U) are IM, then A − B is IM; (d) for every IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) in any U and Hᵈ-a.e. x ∈ M, |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for every d-covector α. The zero current of any degree d in any U is IM: the IMRep with carrier ∅, multiplicity 0 and orientation 0 represents it (∅ is Borel and countably d-rectifiable by Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.countablyRectifiable_of_measure_zero, and every integral or a.e. condition over ∅ holds trivially). The SimonGMT push-forward GeometricCurrentOn.affinePushforward (Simon 6.2.23 for proper affine maps) with boundary_affinePushforward, and exteriorDerivative_affinePullbackForm (d commutes with linear pull-back).
Notation: ι₀ : ℝ^P → ℝ^{P+1}, (ι₀x)_i = x_i (i < P), (ι₀x)_P = 0, a linear isometric embedding (proper); p : ℝ^{P+1} → ℝ^P, (py)_i = y_i (i < P), the orthogonal projection, with ‖p‖ = 1 and p ∘ ι₀ = id. For a linear map L and a form ω, L^#ω(x) := ω(Lx)(L·, …, L·). Let c₀ be the constant of deformation for (P' , m') := (P + 1, m) (valid as m + 1 = P < P + 1) and c := c₀.
1. Push-forward by ι₀. T̃ := ι₀#T ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^{P+1}) (affinePushforward with L = ι₀, b = 0), T̃(ω) = T(ι₀^#ω), and ∂T̃ = ι₀#∂T (boundary_affinePushforward).
2. Properties of T̃. If (M, θ, ξ) is an IMRep of T, then (ι₀(M), θ∘p, (∧ι₀)ξ∘p) is an IMRep of T̃, where (∧ι₀)ζ(α) := ζ(ι₀^*α): ι₀(M) is Borel (ι₀ is a closed embedding) and countably n-rectifiable (Lipschitz image); Hⁿ(ι₀(A)) = Hⁿ(A) for all A (Isometry.hausdorffMeasure_image), hence ∫_{ι₀(M)} g dHⁿ = ∫_M g∘ι₀ dHⁿ; the approximate tangent space of ι₀(M) at ι₀(x) is ι₀(Q) whenever M has approximate tangent space Q at x (blow-ups commute with the isometry ι₀ and Hⁿ is invariant); and (∧ι₀)(±τ₁∧⋯∧τ_n) = ±ι₀τ₁∧⋯∧ι₀τ_n with ι₀τ orthonormal. Then T̃(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω(ι₀x), (∧ι₀)ξ(x)⟩ dHⁿ(x) = ∫_{ι₀(M)} θ(py)⟨ω(y), (∧ι₀)ξ(py)⟩ dHⁿ(y). So T̃ is IM, and likewise ∂T̃ is IM; by (C1), M(T̃) = μ(ι₀(M)) = M(T) and M(∂T̃) = M(∂T). If tsupport ω ∩ ι₀(K) = ∅ then tsupport(ι₀^#ω) ⊆ ι₀⁻¹(tsupport ω) is disjoint from K, so T̃(ω) = 0: T̃ vanishes off the compact ι₀(K).
3. Deformation in ℝ^{P+1}. Apply deformation (with (SL)) to T̃, ρ and K' := ι₀(K): there are s̃, β̃, Π̃, R̃, S̃ with Π̃(η) = Σ_{p∈s̃} β̃_p ∫_{F̃_p} η(y)(e_{ι_p(0)}, …, e_{ι_p(m)}) dHⁿ(y), R̃, S̃ IM, T̃ − Π̃ = ∂R̃ + S̃, (Σ|β̃_p|)ρⁿ ≤ c₀M(T), M(R̃) ≤ c₀ρM(T), M(S̃) ≤ c₀ρM(∂T), cells F̃_p ⊆ K̃ := cthickening(2√(P+1)ρ, ι₀(K)) and R̃, S̃ vanishing off K̃.
4. Cutoff. K̃ is compact; choose a smooth ζ : ℝ^{P+1} → [0, 1] with compact support and ζ = 1 on an open V ⊇ K̃. For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) put ω̃ := ζ·p^#ω, a smooth form with compact support, i.e. ω̃ ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^{P+1}); ω ↦ ω̃ is linear and sequentially continuous for the test-form topologies (derivatives of p^#ω are those of ω composed with the fixed linear map p, and supports lie in the fixed compact tsupport ζ).
5. Evaluation at ω̃. (a) ι₀^#ω̃ = (ζ∘ι₀)·ω because p∘ι₀ = id; since ζ∘ι₀ = 1 on the open set ι₀⁻¹(V) ⊇ K, the form ((ζ∘ι₀) − 1)ω has tsupport disjoint from K, so T̃(ω̃) = T((ζ∘ι₀)ω) = T(ω). (b) On V, ω̃ = p^#ω, so dω̃ = p^#(dω) = 0 on V (dω is an (n+1)-form on the n-dimensional ℝ^P, hence 0); thus tsupport dω̃ ⊆ ℝ^{P+1} ∖ V is disjoint from K̃ and ∂R̃(ω̃) = R̃(dω̃) = 0. (c) As ζ = 1 on every F̃_p ⊆ K̃, Π̃(ω̃) = Σ_{p∈s̃} β̃_p ∫_{F̃_p} ω(py)(p e_{ι_p(0)}, …, p e_{ι_p(m)}) dHⁿ(y). If P ∈ range ι_p ('vertical' cell) one of the vectors is p(e_P) = 0 and the term vanishes. Otherwise range ι_p = {0, …, P − 1}, p e_{ι_p(k)} = e_k, and p maps F̃_p = {y : ρz_i ≤ y_i ≤ ρ(z_i + 1) (i < P), y_P = ρz_P} isometrically onto the cube G_{z'} := ρ(z' + [0, 1]^P) with z' := (z_0, …, z_{P−1}), so ∫_{F̃_p} ω(py)(e_0, …, e_{P−1}) dHⁿ(y) = ∫_{G_{z'}} ω(x)(e_0, …, e_{P−1}) dHⁿ(x). Hence Π̃(ω̃) = Σ_{z'∈s'} β'_{z'} ∫_{G_{z'}} ω(x)(e_0, …, e_{P−1}) dHⁿ(x), where s' is the finite set of z' arising from non-vertical p ∈ s̃ and β'_{z'} := Σ{β̃_p : p ∈ s̃ non-vertical with (z_p)' = z'} ∈ ℤ. (d) Define S(ω) := S̃(ω̃); by step 4, S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P).
6. The currents. By 5(a)–(d) and step 3, T(ω) − Σ_{z'∈s'} β'_{z'} ∫_{G_{z'}} ω(e_0, …, e_{P−1}) dHⁿ = S(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P). Put Π := T − S (contract subtraction), so Π(ω) is the cube sum above, and R := 0 ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(ℝ^P) (IM by the remark above; in fact every (n+1)-current on ℝ^n vanishes). Then T − Π = S = ∂R + S. Take s := {(z', ι) : z' ∈ s'} with ι : Fin n → Fin P the order isomorphism (n = P), β(z', ι) := β'_{z'} and β := 0 elsewhere; F_{(z',ι)} = G_{z'} and the cell formula of the statement holds.
7. IM. Each cube current [[G]](ω) := ∫_G ω(e_0, …, e_{P−1}) dHⁿ is IM: (G, 1, e_0∧⋯∧e_{P−1}) is an IMRep in ℝ^P — G is Borel and countably P-rectifiable, Hᴾ(G) = ρᴾ, and for Hᴾ-a.e. x ∈ G the approximate tangent space of G at x is ℝ^P by (IMC)(a) applied to G ⊆ ℝ^P (ℝ^P has approximate tangent space ℝ^P at every point, Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.hasApproximateTangentSpaceAt_submodule with the submodule ⊤), with the unit orientation e_0∧⋯∧e_{P−1} of the orthonormal standard basis. A finite integer combination of IM currents is IM ((IMC)(c) repeatedly, with X + Y = X − (0 − Y) and 0 IM). So Π is IM, and S = T − Π is IM by (IMC)(c).
8. Estimates. (Σ_{p∈s}|β_p|)ρⁿ ≤ (Σ_{p∈s̃}|β̃_p|)ρⁿ ≤ c₀M(T̃) = cM(T). M(R) = 0. If ω is admissible for M(S) (|ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x), then |ω̃(y)| = ζ(y)|p^*(ω(py))| ≤ |ω(py)| ≤ 1, because p^* maps the orthonormal basis {dx_I} of Λⁿ(ℝ^P) onto part of the orthonormal basis {dy_J} of Λⁿ(ℝ^{P+1}), hence preserves the Euclidean coefficient norm; so S(ω) = S̃(ω̃) ≤ M(S̃) and M(S) ≤ M(S̃) ≤ c₀ρM(∂T̃) = cρM(∂T).
9. Supports. G_{z'} = p(F̃_p) ⊆ p(K̃) ⊆ cthickening(2√(P+1)ρ, K) because p is 1-Lipschitz and p(ι₀(K)) = K. R = 0 vanishes everywhere. If tsupport ω ∩ cthickening(2√(P+1)ρ, K) = ∅ then tsupport ω̃ ⊆ p⁻¹(tsupport ω) is disjoint from K̃ (y ∈ K̃ implies p(y) ∈ cthickening(2√(P+1)ρ, K)), so S(ω) = S̃(ω̃) = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: Embed ℝ^P = ℝ^P × {0} by the linear isometry ι₀ and push T forward (affinePushforward): ι₀#T and its boundary are IM with the same masses and vanish off ι₀(K).
Apply the deformation theorem in ℝ^{P+1} (codimension 1) to ι₀#T.

Test the resulting identity on ζ·p^#ω (p the projection, ζ = 1 near the thickened set): the T-term gives T(ω), the ∂R̃-term vanishes since d(p^#ω) = p^#(dω) = 0, vertical cells drop out, horizontal cells project isometrically to grid cubes.
Π = T − S is an integer cube chain (IM), R = 0, S(ω) = S̃(ζp^#ω) is IM with M(S) ≤ M(S̃) ≤ cρM(∂T); coefficients, cells and supports satisfy the bounds.

For G ⊆ ℝ^P, M_G(X) = X.massOn G is the supremum of max(X(ω), 0) over ω ∈ 𝒟^d(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ G and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x, where |·| is the Euclidean coefficient norm of covectors (covectorEuclideanNorm); M(X) = X.mass = M_U(X). An IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) in U is the contract structure IMRep U d; R represents X when X(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHᵈ for every ω ∈ 𝒟^d(U), where ⟨ω, ξ⟩(x) = ξ(x)(ω(x)); μ_R = θ·Hᵈ⌞M is R.measure; X is integer multiplicity (IM, IsIntegerMultiplicity X) if some IMRep represents it. X vanishes off a set K if X(ω) = 0 for every ω whose tsupport is disjoint from K. X_j ⇀ Y (WeaklyConvergesOn) means X_j(ω) → Y(ω) for every ω. V ⊂⊂ U (CompactlyContained V U) means that closure V is compact and contained in U. Let P, m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, K ⊆ U compact, Λ ∈ [0, ∞) and ε ∈ (0, ∞]. Then there is a finite set 𝒬 ⊆ 𝒟_n(U) such that every IM A ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with ∂A IM, A vanishing off K, M(A) ≤ Λ and M(∂A) ≤ Λ admits Q ∈ 𝒬 and IM currents R ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(U), S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with A(ω) − Q(ω) = ∂R(ω) + S(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) and M(R) + M(S) < ε (masses in [0, ∞]).

Source: step 2 of the parent-supplied proof (Simon Ch. 6, proof of Theorem 7.2, (1)–(3), chapter-06.txt lines 2056–2090), parts (a), (b), (d), (e); part (c) (the case n = P) is the sibling deformation_top. Tools: the siblings deformation (sibling dor_lmb_fc_deformation; for m + 1 < P, radius r(ρ) = 2√P·ρ) and deformation_top (sibling dor_lmb_fc_deformation_top; for m + 1 = P, radius r(ρ) = 2√(P+1)·ρ) both state, under (SL): there is c ≥ 0 such that for every ρ > 0, compact K' ⊆ ℝ^P and IM T ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with ∂T IM and T vanishing off K', there are a finite set s of pairs p = (z_p, ι_p) ∈ ℤ^P × (Fin n → Fin P) with ι_p strictly increasing, integers β_p and Π ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P), IM R ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(ℝ^P), IM S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with Π(ω) = Σ_{p∈s} β_p ∫_{F_p} ω(x)(e_{ι_p(0)}, …, e_{ι_p(m)}) dHⁿ(x) for all ω (F_p := {x : ρz_{p,i} ≤ x_i ≤ ρ(z_{p,i} + 1) for i ∈ range ι_p, x_i = ρz_{p,i} otherwise}), T − Π = ∂R + S, (Σ_{p∈s}|β_p|)·ρⁿ ≤ c·M(T), M(R) ≤ cρ·M(T), M(S) ≤ cρ·M(∂T), F_p ⊆ cthickening(r(ρ), K') for p ∈ s, and R, S vanish off cthickening(r(ρ), K'). Also (C1) the reused accepted sibling dor_imrep_massOn_eq_measure_and_support: for open U, X ∈ 𝒟_d(U) and an IMRep R in U representing X, M_W(X) = μ_R(W) for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P, and spt X = U ∩ spt μ_R. (IMC) the reused accepted sibling cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub: (a) if U is open, M ⊆ M' ⊆ U are Borel and Hᵈ(M' ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, then for Hᵈ-a.e. x ∈ M and every linear subspace Q, M has approximate tangent space Q at x iff M' has (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt d · x Q); (b) if U is open, R = (M, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in U and E is Borel, there are A ∈ 𝒟_d(U) and an IMRep R' in U with carrier M ∩ E, multiplicity θ and orientation ξ that represents A (so μ_{R'} = μ_R⌞E); (c) if U is open and A, B ∈ 𝒟_d(U) are IM, then A − B is IM; (d) for every IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) in any U and Hᵈ-a.e. x ∈ M, |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for every d-covector α. The zero current of any degree d in any U is IM: the IMRep with carrier ∅, multiplicity 0 and orientation 0 represents it (∅ is Borel and countably d-rectifiable by Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.countablyRectifiable_of_measure_zero, and every integral or a.e. condition over ∅ holds trivially).
0. The case n > P. An alternating n-linear map on the P-dimensional space ℝ^P vanishes when n > P (any n vectors are linearly dependent, AlternatingMap.map_linearDependent), so every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) is the zero form and every A ∈ 𝒟_n(U) is the zero current. Take 𝒬 := {0}; for any A use Q := 0, R := 0, S := 0 (IM by the remark above): A(ω) − Q(ω) = 0 = ∂R(ω) + S(ω) and M(R) + M(S) = 0 < ε. From now on n ≤ P, and DEF denotes deformation if n < P and deformation_top if n = P, with its constant c and radius r(ρ).
1. Choice of ρ. Choose ρ > 0 with 2·c·ρ·Λ < ε (in [0, ∞]; possible as Λ < ∞ and ε > 0: ρ := 1 if cΛ = 0, otherwise ρ := min(ε, 1)/(4cΛ) with ε read in (0, ∞]). Put K_r := cthickening(r(ρ), K), a compact set.
2. The finite set 𝒬. Let 𝒞 be the set of p = (z, ι) ∈ ℤ^P × (Fin n → Fin P) with ι strictly increasing and F_p ⊆ K_r. 𝒞 is finite: (Fin n → Fin P) is finite, and ρz ∈ F_p ⊆ K_r with K_r bounded, so each |z_i| ≤ sup_{y∈K_r}|y|/ρ. Let B := ⌊cΛ/ρⁿ⌋ ∈ ℕ. Let 𝒬 be the set of X ∈ 𝒟_n(U) for which there are s ⊆ 𝒞 and integers b_p (p ∈ s) with |b_p| ≤ B and X(ω) = Σ_{p∈s} b_p ∫_{F_p} ω(x)(e_{ι_p(0)}, …, e_{ι_p(m)}) dHⁿ(x) for all ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). A current is determined by its values (GeometricCurrentOn.ext) and there are finitely many data (s, (b_p)_{p∈s}), so 𝒬 is finite (Set.Finite.of_finite_image along X ↦ (ω ↦ X ω)).
3. Extension by zero (parent step 2(a)). Let A be as in the statement, R_A = (M, θ, ξ) an IMRep of A and R_∂ = (M', θ', ξ') an IMRep of ∂A.
 (a) U ∖ K is open and A vanishes on every form supported in it, so by (C1) μ_{R_A}(U ∖ K) = M_{U∖K}(A) = 0; as θ ≥ 1 on M ⊆ U this gives Hⁿ(M ∖ K) = 0. ∂A also vanishes off K (if tsupport ω ∩ K = ∅ then tsupport dω ∩ K = ∅ and ∂A(ω) = A(dω) = 0), so likewise H^m(M' ∖ K) = 0.
 (b) By (IMC)(b) with E := K (closed, hence Borel) the data (M ∩ K, θ, ξ) form an IMRep in U. The same data form an IMRep R̂ in univ: the carrier is ⊆ univ, and for compact K'' ⊆ ℝ^P, ∫_{M∩K∩K''} θ dHⁿ ≤ ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ by the local integrability of R_A on the compact K ⊆ U; the other fields are unchanged. By (IMC)(b) in univ with E := univ there is Ǎ ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) represented by an IMRep with carrier M ∩ K ∩ univ = M ∩ K and the same multiplicity and orientation, hence by R̂. Thus Ǎ is IM, Ǎ vanishes off K (its carrier lies in K), and for ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (also a test form on ℝ^P) Ǎ(ω) = ∫_{M∩K} θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ = ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ = A(ω) by (a). By (C1) (in univ and in U), M(Ǎ) = μ_{R̂}(ℝ^P) = μ_{R_A}(K) ≤ μ_{R_A}(U) = M(A) ≤ Λ.
 (c) The same construction for ∂A gives an IM Ž ∈ 𝒟_m(ℝ^P) represented by (M' ∩ K, θ', ξ'), vanishing off K, with Ž(ω) = ∂A(ω) for ω ∈ 𝒟^m(U) and M(Ž) ≤ M(∂A) ≤ Λ.
 (d) ∂Ǎ = Ž. Choose a smooth ζ with compact support in U and ζ = 1 on an open V ⊇ K (finitely many smooth bumps exists_contDiff_tsupport_subset covering K, combined by a partition of unity). For ω ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P), ζω ∈ 𝒟^m(U) and d(ζω) = dω on V (d is local and ζω = ω on V). As the carriers lie in K ⊆ V: ∂Ǎ(ω) = Ǎ(dω) = ∫_{M∩K} θ⟨dω, ξ⟩ = ∫_{M∩K} θ⟨d(ζω), ξ⟩ = Ǎ(d(ζω)) = A(d(ζω)) = ∂A(ζω) = Ž(ζω) = ∫_{M'∩K} θ'⟨ζω, ξ'⟩ = ∫_{M'∩K} θ'⟨ω, ξ'⟩ = Ž(ω). So ∂Ǎ = Ž is IM and M(∂Ǎ) ≤ Λ.
4. Deformation (parent step 2(b)/(c)). Apply DEF (with the antecedent (SL)) to Ǎ, ρ and K' := K. It gives s, β, Π, R̂, Ŝ with: ι_p strictly increasing and F_p ⊆ K_r for p ∈ s, so s ⊆ 𝒞; Π(ω) = Σ_{p∈s} β_p ∫_{F_p} ω(x)(e_{ι_p(0)}, …, e_{ι_p(m)}) dHⁿ for all ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P); (Σ_{p∈s}|β_p|)ρⁿ ≤ cM(Ǎ) ≤ cΛ, so |β_p| ≤ B; R̂, Ŝ IM; Ǎ − Π = ∂R̂ + Ŝ; M(R̂) ≤ cρM(Ǎ) ≤ cρΛ and M(Ŝ) ≤ cρM(∂Ǎ) ≤ cρΛ.
5. Restriction to U (parent step 2(d)). Q := Π.restrictDomain (U ⊆ univ), R := R̂.restrictDomain, S := Ŝ.restrictDomain. By step 4, Q ∈ 𝒬 (data s and b_p := β_p). R and S are IM: if (N, ϑ, η) is an IMRep of R̂ in univ, (IMC)(b) in univ with E := U gives an IMRep with carrier N ∩ U; the same data form an IMRep in U (carrier ⊆ U, local integrability on compact subsets of U inherited) which represents R because every ω ∈ 𝒟^{n+1}(U) vanishes outside U, so ∫_N ϑ⟨ω, η⟩ = ∫_{N∩U} ϑ⟨ω, η⟩; the same for S. For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U): A(ω) − Q(ω) = Ǎ(ω) − Π(ω) = R̂(dω) + Ŝ(ω) = ∂R(ω) + S(ω). Every form admissible for M(R) = M_U(R) is, regarded in ℝ^P, admissible for M(R̂) with the same value, so M(R) ≤ M(R̂) and likewise M(S) ≤ M(Ŝ). Hence M(R) + M(S) ≤ 2cρΛ < ε by step 1. ∎
proof_key_steps: If n > P every n-form on ℝ^P vanishes, so all currents are 0 and 𝒬 = {0} works.
Pick ρ with 2cρΛ < ε; the integer polyhedral chains on the finitely many grid cells inside cthickening(r(ρ), K) with coefficients ≤ cΛ/ρⁿ form a finite set 𝒬.
Extend A and ∂A by zero to IM currents Ǎ, Ž on ℝ^P (C1 shows the carriers lie a.e. in K; (IMC)(b) gives the currents) and check ∂Ǎ = Ž with a cutoff.
Apply the deformation theorem (n < P) or its top-dimensional case (n = P) to Ǎ: Ǎ − Π = ∂R̂ + Ŝ with Π a chain in 𝒬 and small M(R̂), M(Ŝ).
Restrict R̂, Ŝ, Π to U: restrictions stay IM, masses do not increase, and A − Q = ∂R + S with M(R) + M(S) ≤ 2cρΛ < ε.
